findings.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages: Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 over-counts by one page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, producing a phantom empty last page; should be Math.ceil(user_count/limit)

Pagination race in next/previous + findMembers: out-of-order AJAX responses clobber state (no sequence token, abort, or stale-response check), causing pager label and member content to desync when clicks happen quickly
Public group members page truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls added, regressing from the previous 200-member limit so groups with more than 50 members show no way to see the rest

remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) directly, bypassing Group#remove and skipping GroupUser destroy callbacks/counter caches; the subsequent group.save is a no-op making the render_json_error branch dead
addMembers never clears the usernames input after Add, so repeated clicks re-submit the same usernames; server-side add_members has no dedup check and can create duplicate GroupUser rows
findMembers returns undefined (bare return instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([])) when name is empty, breaking the promise contract for any future caller chaining .then

Unbounded `limit` parameter in groups_controller.rb members action allows any signed-in user to request limit=100000000 (or negative limit, which PostgreSQL treats as no limit), forcing the server to load and serialize the entire group membership, causing memory/CPU exhaustion and an easy DoS vector — needs a server-side clamp

Unbounded input in admin/groups_controller.rb add_members: params.require(:usernames) is split with no cap on element count, allowing an admin session to submit tens of thousands of usernames in one request, producing a long-running request that holds a save transaction open

N+1 query shape in admin/groups_controller.rb add_members: one User.find_by_username query per username (plus inserts and group.save) instead of a single WHERE username IN (...) lookup — a regression from the previous batched group.usernames= assignment
total = group.users.count adds a second full-table count per request in groups_controller.rb members action, compounding cost when combined with the unbounded limit

totalPages computed property in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing an off-by-one extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50 yields 3 pages instead of 2) — should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), causing spurious server requests for empty pages

Public /groups/:name/members response shape changed from bare JSON array to enveloped object { members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }, breaking external API consumers, theme components, and plugins that iterate the response as an array

Default/only page size for /groups/:name/members changed from 200 (automatic groups) or full unpaginated list (non-automatic groups) to a hard default of 50, so consumers relying on 'returns all members' will silently see only 50

POST /admin/groups request contract changed from nested group[name]/group[visible]/group[usernames] payload to flat top-level params, causing existing consumers posting group: {name: ..., usernames: ...} to create groups with blank names (silent corruption instead of a clean 400)
Membership-at-create via POST /admin/groups is no longer possible since usernames support was dropped entirely
PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id contract changed from nested params[:group] payload to flat top-level params, breaking existing consumers
PATCH incremental-membership path (changes: {add:, delete:}) removed from admin groups update with no replacement, breaking incremental-membership integrations

Existing consumers sending PUT group: {visible: "true"} will silently flip the group's visible flag to false (and silently drop alias_level/name changes) while returning success_json, causing silent data mutation of an existing resource

totalPages formula Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is wrong for exact multiples of limit (yields 3 pages for user_count=100, limit=50), so 'next' stays enabled on the real last page and clicking it renders an empty member list
showingLast never becomes true on the real last page when member count is an exact multiple of limit, because totalPages is inflated
add_members splits usernames with commas without trimming whitespace, so 'bob, alice' fails to find ' alice' due to exact-match find_by_username
add_members silently skips nonexistent usernames and returns success_json even when zero members were added, making success indistinguishable from a no-op

The automatic-group protection for remove_member is effectively untested due to the wrong HTTP verb in the test

Routes call model.findMembers() fire-and-forget instead of chaining in afterModel, so rejected AJAX calls (403 for hidden group, network error) leave the member list permanently empty with no error surfaced

Client/server route mismatch: routes are declared collection-scoped inside resources :groups (DELETE|PUT /admin/groups/members) but the client calls /admin/groups/{id}/members.json, causing 404 RoutingError on every add/remove member request; controller specs bypass routing so they pass while the feature is broken end-to-end

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination race in next/previous + findMembers: out-of-order AJAX responses clobber state (no sequence token, abort, or stale-response check), causing pager label and member content to desync when clicks happen quickly
Public group members page truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls added, regressing from the previous 200-member limit so groups with more than 50 members show no way to see the rest

adjudication.rationale: The public `GroupsController#members` endpoint now always paginates with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` (previously non-automatic groups were not limited, and automatic groups defaulted to 200). The public route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` calls `model.findMembers()` but no pagination UI/actions were added in `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` (it just iterates `{{#each m in members}}`). So groups with >50 members will only show the first 50 with no navigation controls in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) directly, bypassing Group#remove and skipping GroupUser destroy callbacks/counter caches; the subsequent group.save is a no-op making the render_json_error branch dead

adjudication.rationale:
In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else ...`.

`group.users.delete(user_id)` removes the association directly rather than going through a domain method like `group.remove(user)` (which is used elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. older controller logic and is invoked from the JS model via `removeMember`). Using `delete` can bypass join-model `destroy` callbacks and any counter-cache/touch behavior that would run on `destroy`/custom remove logic.

Also, calling `group.save` immediately afterward is likely redundant because no group attributes are being modified in this method; therefore the `render_json_error` branch is unlikely to ever be exercised (though not provably impossible if validations could fail). This is a concrete maintainability/logic concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior in this app.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the usernames input after Add, so repeated clicks re-submit the same usernames; server-side add_members has no dedup check and can create duplicate GroupUser rows

adjudication.rationale: The client-side action `addMembers` explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.get("usernames")` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`, so repeated clicks can resend the same usernames (admin-group.js.es6). However, the claim that this will create duplicate `GroupUser` rows is not verifiable from the diff: `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` loops `group.add(user)` without an explicit dedup check, but whether duplicates can be created depends on model/DB constraints and `group.add` implementation not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `limit` parameter in groups_controller.rb members action allows any signed-in user to request limit=100000000 (or negative limit, which PostgreSQL treats as no limit), forcing the server to load and serialize the entire group membership, causing memory/CPU exhaustion and an easy DoS vector — needs a server-side clamp

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff adds `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no server-side clamp or validation. This allows a caller to pass an extremely large `limit` or a negative value; in PostgreSQL, `LIMIT -1` effectively removes the limit, which can force loading/serializing the entire group membership (`serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer)`) and create a DoS risk. The finding is directly supported by the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded input in admin/groups_controller.rb add_members: params.require(:usernames) is split with no cap on element count, allowing an admin session to submit tens of thousands of usernames in one request, producing a long-running request that holds a save transaction open

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, which does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then iterates `usernames.split(",").each` with no cap or validation on length/count. That allows a single request to attempt adding an arbitrarily large number of usernames, resulting in potentially very long processing time and heavy DB work (looping `User.find_by_username` + `group.add(user)` many times) before `group.save`, creating a realistic performance/DoS risk within an admin session.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query shape in admin/groups_controller.rb add_members: one User.find_by_username query per username (plus inserts and group.save) instead of a single WHERE username IN (...) lookup — a regression from the previous batched group.usernames= assignment

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop `User.find_by_username(username)` is executed for each username, followed by `group.add(user)`. This is a classic per-item query pattern (N lookups for N usernames), whereas the prior code path used `group.usernames = ...` (removed in this diff) which likely handled membership assignment more efficiently. This is a performance/regression concern (query shape), not a functional correctness defect visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: total = group.users.count adds a second full-table count per request in groups_controller.rb members action, compounding cost when combined with the unbounded limit

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` and still fetches the page via `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`, so it adds an additional COUNT query per request to return `meta.total`. That can be a performance concern for large groups. However, the finding’s claim about an “unbounded limit” is not supported by the diff: `limit` defaults to 50 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`), though it is still user-supplied and not capped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed property in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing an off-by-one extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50 yields 3 pages instead of 2) — should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), causing spurious server requests for empty pages

Public /groups/:name/members response shape changed from bare JSON array to enveloped object { members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }, breaking external API consumers, theme components, and plugins that iterate the response as an array

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the /groups/:group_id/members response from a bare serialized array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`) to an enveloped object with `members` and `meta` (`render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` in `GroupsController#members`). That is a backward-incompatible API change for any callers expecting an array, but the diff also updates first-party client code (`Discourse.Group#findMembers` now reads `result.members`/`result.meta`) to match it. The claim about breaking “external API consumers, theme components, and plugins” is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default/only page size for /groups/:name/members changed from 200 (automatic groups) or full unpaginated list (non-automatic groups) to a hard default of 50, so consumers relying on 'returns all members' will silently see only 50

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `GroupsController#members` now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` for all groups and always does `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned the full unpaginated list and automatic groups defaulted to 200 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 200)`). This is an intentional pagination/API behavior change (also reflected by new `meta` in the JSON response and UI paging), but it is a potentially breaking change for any consumers assuming the endpoint returns all members by default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: POST /admin/groups request contract changed from nested group[name]/group[visible]/group[usernames] payload to flat top-level params, causing existing consumers posting group: {name: ..., usernames: ...} to create groups with blank names (silent corruption instead of a clean 400)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the POST /admin/groups parameter contract: Admin::GroupsController#create now reads top-level params[:name]/params[:visible] (and no longer params[:group][:name]/params[:group][:visible]/params[:group][:usernames]), while the JS client was updated accordingly (Group#asJSON now returns flat keys and Group#create posts that). This is a backwards-incompatible API change for any existing consumers still sending a nested `group: { ... }` payload. However, the specific claim of “silent corruption creating groups with blank names” is not directly verifiable from the diff because whether a blank name can be saved depends on Group model validations not shown here; the controller will at least route failures through `render_json_error` if `group.save` fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Membership-at-create via POST /admin/groups is no longer possible since usernames support was dropped entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes usernames-from-create support: `Discourse.Group#create()` now POSTs only `{name, alias_level, visible}` (no usernames) and `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` only, whereas the previous implementation accepted `params[:group][:usernames]`. Membership changes are now handled via new `PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (`add_members`) after the group has an id (UI shows add-members only under `{{#if id}}`). So “membership-at-create via POST /admin/groups is no longer possible” is correct, but it’s an intentional API/behavior change rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT/PATCH /admin/groups/:id contract changed from nested params[:group] payload to flat top-level params, breaking existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the Admin::GroupsController parameter contract. Previously, update/create consumed a nested payload (e.g. `payload = params[:group]` and `params[:group][:name]`), but now `create` and `update` read top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`) and the JS client was updated to send flat JSON via `Group#asJSON`. This is a real API/contract change that could break existing external consumers, but it’s not inherently a correctness defect within the PR since the in-repo caller was updated accordingly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH incremental-membership path (changes: {add:, delete:}) removed from admin groups update with no replacement, breaking incremental-membership integrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-based incremental membership update path: `Admin::GroupsController` no longer branches on `request.patch?` and the old `update_patch` implementation that processed `params[:changes][:add]` / `[:delete]` is deleted. The corresponding spec coverage for incremental PATCH updates is also removed. While new dedicated endpoints exist (`put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), callers still using the previous PATCH `changes` contract would now be ignored by `update`, so this is a backward-incompatible API change/integration risk rather than an internal correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing consumers sending PUT group: {visible: "true"} will silently flip the group's visible flag to false (and silently drop alias_level/name changes) while returning success_json, causing silent data mutation of an existing resource

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the params shape changed from nested `params[:group]` to top-level params, but `visible` is now always assigned: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. If an existing client still sends `PUT /admin/groups/:id` with `{ group: { visible: "true" } }`, then `params[:visible]` is nil and this code will set `visible` to `false` (silent mutation). `alias_level` and `name` are only updated from top-level `params[:alias_level]`/`params[:name]`, so nested values would be ignored. The action can still return `success_json` after `group.save`, making the breakage silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages formula Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 is wrong for exact multiples of limit (yields 3 pages for user_count=100, limit=50), so 'next' stays enabled on the real last page and clicking it renders an empty member list

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. For exact multiples of `limit` (e.g. `user_count=100`, `limit=50`), this yields 3 instead of 2. Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, page 2 will not be considered the last page, leaving the `next` action enabled. The `next` action then sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` which becomes `100`, and `Group.findMembers()` requests `offset=100`, returning an empty member list (server uses `limit(...).offset(offset)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: showingLast never becomes true on the real last page when member count is an exact multiple of limit, because totalPages is inflated

adjudication.rationale: `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3 pages instead of 2). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, it will not become true on the actual last non-empty page. The `next` action can also set `offset` to `user_count`, making `currentPage` advance to the inflated page number and potentially fetching an empty member list (`offset=100` for 100 users).

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members splits usernames with commas without trimming whitespace, so 'bob, alice' fails to find ' alice' due to exact-match find_by_username

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)`. There is no `strip`/whitespace normalization on each token, so input like `"bob, alice"` produces `" alice"`, which will not match an existing username via exact lookup. This endpoint is newly added/used by the UI (`Group#addMembers` sends the raw `usernames` string), so the diff introduces/exposes this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips nonexistent usernames and returns success_json even when zero members were added, making success indistinguishable from a no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is looked up with `User.find_by_username`; missing users are simply ignored (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`). Regardless of whether any users were found/added, it still calls `group.save` and will typically render `success_json` (unless validation fails), so a request where all usernames are nonexistent can return success indistinguishable from adding members. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior concern, but the diff doesn’t establish that an error/diagnostic is required by spec, and similar “silent skip” behavior existed previously in `update_patch`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test for remove_member on automatic groups uses PUT instead of DELETE verb, so the request matches add_members route and raises ActionController::ParameterMissing instead of exercising the automatic-group protection path
The automatic-group protection for remove_member is effectively untested due to the wrong HTTP verb in the test

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the automatic-group guard test under `.remove_member` uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, but the routes wire `remove_member` to `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (`config/routes.rb`: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). While Rails controller specs invoke the action directly (so the guard `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic` in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` will still run), the test does not exercise the verb/route that real clients use, so it can mask routing/verb regressions and is misaligned with the API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined (not a promise) on the empty-name path, so callers chaining .then will throw

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Discourse.Group#findMembers` to `return;` when the group name is empty (so it returns `undefined`), but all call sites shown in this diff were also changed to stop chaining promises: both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` removed `findMembers().then(...)` and now just call `model.findMembers();`. No remaining `.then` chaining on `findMembers` is visible in the provided diff, so the claim that callers chaining `.then` will throw is not verifiable from this PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Routes call model.findMembers() fire-and-forget instead of chaining in afterModel, so rejected AJAX calls (403 for hidden group, network error) leave the member list permanently empty with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `afterModel` hooks that returned/chained `model.findMembers()` (admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6) and replaces them with `model.findMembers();` called in `setupController` without returning the promise. `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs an AJAX request and only sets `members` inside `.then(...)`; on rejection (e.g., 403 from `GroupsController#members` due to `guardian.ensure_can_see!`, or network error), `members` never gets set and there is no error handling in the route/controller, so the UI can remain empty with no surfaced error. Previously, returning the promise from `afterModel` would at least propagate rejection to the route transition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client/server route mismatch: routes are declared collection-scoped inside resources :groups (DELETE|PUT /admin/groups/members) but the client calls /admin/groups/{id}/members.json, causing 404 RoutingError on every add/remove member request; controller specs bypass routing so they pass while the feature is broken end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared *inside* `resources :groups` but **not** inside a `collection do ... end` block, so they are member-scoped and generate paths like `/admin/groups/:group_id/members(.:format)`. This matches the client calls in `Discourse.Group#addMembers`/`removeMember` (`/admin/groups/` + id + `/members.json`). Therefore the claimed client/server route mismatch (and resulting 404s) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, producing a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50), this returns 3 instead of 2, so `showingLast` (propertyEqual currentPage/totalPages) stays false on the real last page and the `next` action can advance `offset` to `user_count`, leading `findMembers()` to request an empty page (`offset` becomes `user_count`). Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` would avoid the phantom last page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently ignores unknown usernames (and usernames with whitespace due to missing .strip, so "bob, alice" drops " alice") and still returns success_json, giving the user no feedback about invalid entries

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and looks up `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. This means inputs like `"bob, alice"` will try to find `" alice"` and fail, silently skipping that entry. It also silently ignores any unknown usernames (the `if user = ...` guard) and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, providing no indication that some/all requested adds were invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rejection handling on any of the new AJAX member operations: removeMember and addMembers swallow server 422/500/network errors with no user feedback, and findMembers is called fire-and-forget so a failed load renders an empty member table with no error state

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new AJAX-driven member operations without any local error handling: `admin-group.js.es6` actions `addMembers` and `removeMember` call `model.addMembers(...)` / `model.removeMember(...)` but do not attach any `.catch`/failure UI (they just return the promise). Likewise both routes (`admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) call `model.findMembers();` “fire-and-forget” instead of returning/awaiting it, and templates render `{{each member in members}}`; if the request fails, `members` will remain unset/empty and there is no explicit error state. This is a concrete, diff-grounded UX/robustness concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove errors are fully swallowed globally or that this necessarily breaks correctness in all cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination race: rapid next/previous clicks fire concurrent findMembers requests without cancellation/serialization, so out-of-order responses can overwrite newer ones and display the wrong page; offset clamping against stale user_count compounds the drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pagination actions (`next`/`previous`) that update `group.offset` and immediately call `group.findMembers()` (admin-group.js.es6). `findMembers()` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and then unconditionally `setProperties({ ... offset: result.meta.offset, members: ... })` on the model (group.js). There is no request cancellation, no sequencing token, and no guard to ignore stale responses, so rapid clicks can create multiple in-flight requests whose responses may arrive out of order and overwrite newer page state (wrong `members`/`offset` displayed). The actions also compute the next offset using current `group.get("user_count")`, which can be stale relative to what the server will return, potentially compounding page drift when combined with out-of-order updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), which bypasses GroupUser callbacks and counter-cache bookkeeping, leaving groups.user_count stale since the subsequent group.save does not recompute it; this corrupts the index serialization, header display, and totalPages math

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff changes member removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` (no longer using the prior `group.remove(user)` logic that existed in the removed `update_patch` path). Association `delete` removes the join row directly and will bypass any custom bookkeeping in `Group#remove` / join-model callbacks (e.g., updating a cached `user_count`). The subsequent `group.save` in this method does not recompute membership counts. Since `user_count` is serialized in admin group listings (BasicGroupSerializer output includes `user_count` per the spec) and is used in the admin UI for paging math (`totalPages` in admin-group.js.es6), a stale counter would produce incorrect displays/pagination until recomputed elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#members changed its response contract to an envelope {members, meta:{total, limit, offset}} with pagination applied to all groups, but no spec covers the envelope shape, limit/offset application, default limit of 50 vs old 200, or the behavioral change paginating non-automatic groups (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-33)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to an explicit JSON envelope `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and applies `limit`/`offset` to *all* groups with a new default `limit` of 50 (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-33). The PR also updates the client to consume this via `Group#findMembers` expecting `result.meta` and `result.members`. However, the only specs touched are `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`; there is no coverage added for the non-admin `GroupsController#members` response shape or pagination behavior, so the finding about missing spec coverage for the new contract/pagination is grounded. This is a test/contract-coverage gap rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group rename on non-automatic groups lost its test: the old 'is able to update group members' test verifying PUT #update with name 'fred' was deleted, leaving the group.name = params[:name] if !group.automatic path (line 30) completely uncovered so a regression dropping renaming or applying it to automatic groups would pass CI (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#update now handles renaming via `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic`, but the specs no longer cover renaming for a non-automatic group. The previous `.update` spec that asserted `group.name.should == 'fred'` was removed, and the remaining `.update` context only tests that automatic groups ignore name changes. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage that could allow a regression in non-automatic renaming behavior to pass CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No regression test asserting that sending usernames/changes to PUT #update no longer modifies membership, and the old incremental context tests (add/delete/nonexistent-user/no-op) were deleted and not re-homed against the new add_members/remove_member endpoints (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24-39)

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves membership mutation out of `Admin::GroupsController#update` (now only sets `alias_level`, `visible`, and `name`; no `usernames`/`changes` handling) and into new endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member` (see `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb`). In the spec, the prior `.update` membership tests (including the “incremental” add/delete/nonexistent/no-op cases) were deleted, and the new `.add_members`/`.remove_member` contexts only cover adding several users and removing an existing member, plus automatic-group rejection, but do not re-home the old edge-case behaviors. There is also no regression test asserting that passing legacy membership params to PUT `#update` no longer changes membership.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames and gives no client feedback, the old 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' test was deleted and not restored, and usernames are not stripped so 'bob, alice' with a space fails to match 'alice' — no test pins down either the silent-failure UX or the whitespace bug (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:56-69)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` passes each raw token to `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. This makes inputs like `"bob, alice"` attempt to look up `" alice"`, which will not match `alice`, so valid users can fail to be added. The method also unconditionally returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, even if some/most usernames were unknown and skipped, providing no feedback. The spec coverage for silently skipping unknown users (previously present under incremental patch updates) is gone and not replaced for `add_members`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one: totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields 2 pages when user_count is exactly 50 with limit 50, so showingLast never becomes true on page 1 and navigating to page 2 shows an empty list; no unit tests cover currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast (including zero-member, exact-multiple, offset-clamping cases) and no server-side test covers offset >= total (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:5-13)
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying pagination bug: when the total number of users is an exact multiple of the page size, the logic allows navigating to a next page where offset == total/user_count, resulting in an empty list and confusing UX on the last page. The candidate attributes it to totalPages/showingLast/off-by-one calculations but the effect and scenario match the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member has no test for removing a user_id not in the group (silently succeeds via group.users.delete), a nonexistent group_id causes Group.find to raise an unhandled 500 (add_members has the same gap), and no test catches that group.users.delete mutates the association before group.save so a failed save leaves the member already removed while returning an error (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, .remove_member context)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member, both using `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)` (will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` if invalid) and `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save`. The new specs in `.remove_member` only cover automatic-group rejection and successful removal; they do not cover removing a non-member user_id or invalid group_id. Also, because `group.users.delete(user_id)` executes the deletion immediately (not contingent on `group.save`), a hypothetical `group.save` failure would still leave the member removed while returning an error—this transactional inconsistency is a concrete edge-case concern introduced by this implementation, even if actual save failures may be rare/unknown from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The remove_member automatic-group test uses xhr :put but the route is delete 'members', so controller specs bypassing the router never verify the DELETE verb actually routes to remove_member; a routing regression (e.g., DELETE mapping to add_members) would go undetected. Additionally, the create failure path (invalid/duplicate group name → render_json_error) is untested
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the remove_member test issues an xhr :put while the route is defined with DELETE for 'members' => groups#remove_member, meaning the test doesn’t verify correct HTTP verb/routing. Extra notes about other untested paths don’t change the match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No client-side QUnit tests for the new next/previous actions, findMembers offset clamping (Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))), removeMember, or addMembers flows; also findMembers returns a promise that mutates model state via setProperties but the admin route fires it in setupController without returning the promise, so rendering happens against stale/empty state with no error handling (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6, app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js)
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate explicitly notes that `findMembers` now returns a promise and is invoked from the admin route/controller in `setupController` without returning/awaiting/handling it, so rendering can occur before member data is available (stale/empty state) and there’s no error handling—i.e., the same unhandled async/race condition described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination math in totalPages produces an empty phantom last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (should use Math.ceil instead of Math.floor + 1); currentPage has the same flaw

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` and `currentPage` as `Math.floor(offset / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50), `totalPages` becomes 3 instead of 2, creating a phantom last page. This is reachable because the `next` action sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, allowing `offset == user_count`, and then `group.findMembers()` will request that offset and can return an empty member list while `currentPage` shows the extra page. Using `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)` (and clamping `offset` to `user_count - limit`) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 with no pagination UI since members.hbs template got no pager controls (next/previous exist only in admin controller)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`) and returns `{members, meta}` instead of all members. On the client, the public route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()` with no UI/actions to change `offset`, and the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` simply iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pager controls. Since `Discourse.Group#findMembers` defaults `limit: 50, offset: 0`, the public members list will display only the first 50 members with no pagination UI to reach the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New test exercises remove_member with xhr :put instead of DELETE, so the DELETE route wiring and remove_member automatic-group path are effectively untested; also implicit fixture coupling on group id 1 being automatic

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` example calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the diff wires `remove_member` to the DELETE verb (`config/routes.rb`: `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). So the spec is not exercising the intended DELETE route. Additionally, hardcoding `group_id: 1` assumes an automatic group with id 1 exists, which is implicit fixture/seed coupling rather than setting up the needed automatic group in the test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently swallows unknown/malformed usernames: no strip, no blank rejection, nonexistent usernames skipped while response is unconditionally success_json

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` succeeds; otherwise it silently does nothing (no `strip`, no blank rejection, no error/partial failure reporting). It still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero members were actually added. This behavior is verifiable in the diff, but it may be an intentional UX/API choice (similar silent skipping existed in the prior incremental update code), so it’s not clearly a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fire-and-forget promises across the whole members flow: findMembers/addMembers/removeMember calls drop the promise with no error path, so failed AJAX leaves the member list stale/empty with zero feedback

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce several fire-and-forget async calls in the members flow: both routes call `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting the promise (`admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), and the admin controller’s `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without returning/handling the promise. In `removeMember`, the inner `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` promise is also ignored. Additionally, `findMembers/addMembers/removeMember` have only success `.then(...)` paths and no `.catch(...)`/error feedback. However, nothing in the diff proves this causes a definite broken behavior (Ember will still re-render when `members` is set on success), so it’s best classified as a robustness/UX/flow concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TODO comment documents that usernames input is never cleared after adding, enabling duplicate submissions via double-click or re-submission after invisible failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `addMembers` with a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment, and the action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `usernames` afterward (admin-group.js.es6). The template keeps binding the user selector to `usernames` (group.hbs), so the input will remain populated and can be resubmitted (e.g., double-click). Whether this causes true duplication/errors server-side isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the UX/flow issue is real and explicitly acknowledged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group-selector component reduced to a dead, unbound bare input with no value binding or wiring; it's non-functional leftover WIP that breaks any consumer silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/components/admin-group-selector.hbs` only removes surrounding blank lines; the actual template content remains the same single `<input type="text">` both before and after. There is no change that "reduced" it or removed bindings/wiring in this PR, so the finding is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/misleading error branch in remove_member: group.users.delete mutates the join table directly so group.save can never fail, making the render_json_error branch dead code

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, `group.users.delete(user_id)` acts on the association and will persist the join-table change immediately; the subsequent `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)` is therefore likely redundant and the failure branch is at least misleading (and may be effectively dead in normal operation), since no group attributes are modified in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination/UI state (limit, offset, members) stored on the shared Discourse.Group domain model with clamping logic duplicated in two places instead of centralized

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves pagination/UI state onto the shared `Discourse.Group` model (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count`, and `members` set in `findMembers()` in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`). The admin controller then adds its own pagination computations and also clamps offsets in `actions.next/previous` (`Math.min/Math.max` in `admin-group.js.es6`), while `Group.findMembers()` independently clamps `offset` again (`var ... offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`). This is a real, diff-grounded design/duplication concern (logic split between controller and model, and model now holds view-ish state), but it’s not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent return contract on findMembers: empty-name early exit changed from returning Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) to bare return, so callers sometimes get a promise and sometimes undefined

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Discourse.Group#findMembers` from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` on empty name to a bare `return` (`if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`), while the non-empty path still returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise. That makes the method’s return type inconsistent (promise vs `undefined`). In this diff, the previous `.then(...)`-based callers in `afterModel` were removed and current callers just invoke `model.findMembers();` without chaining, so it’s not a directly verifiable runtime break here, but it is a real API/contract regression that could trip future/other callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs item template reaches outside its item context via implicit fallback lookup for 'automatic' and relies on fragile Ember action bubbling for removeMember

adjudication.rationale: `group_member.hbs` uses `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}` even though the item view (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) defines no `automatic` property and the each-loop supplies `member` as the item. That makes the `automatic` check depend on implicit/fallback lookup outside the item context; if it resolves to `undefined`/falsey, the remove link will render even for automatic groups (which are not allowed to be modified, per `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` returning 422 for `group.automatic`). The `{{action "removeMember" member}}` also depends on default action targeting/bubbling to reach the controller action defined in `admin-group.js.es6`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb silently succeeds for nonexistent or whitespace-padded usernames — missing users are skipped without error and the endpoint still renders success_json, so admins believe members were added when they were not (also missing .strip on usernames unlike create's group name handling)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code `usernames.split(",").each` only adds when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user, otherwise it does nothing and still renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. It also does not `strip` per-username tokens, so whitespace-padded entries would be skipped. However, the diff shows similar prior behavior existed (the removed spec cases explicitly asserted silent success for non-existent users), so this is more an API/UX semantics concern than a clear defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: totalPages in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(count/limit)+1, producing a phantom empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil — also makes showingLast wrong so 'next' stays enabled and leads to a blank member list

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50), this yields an extra page (3 instead of 2). Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to this inflated `totalPages`, the UI will consider the true last page not-last, leaving “next” enabled. Clicking “next” sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, which can become exactly `user_count`, and `findMembers()` then requests that offset, producing an empty `members` list (blank page). Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with appropriate zero handling) would avoid the phantom page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Stale-response race in admin-group.js.es6 pagination (next/previous) and findMembers — in-flight requests are not cancelled or serialized, so an older response can overwrite newer state and revert the UI to an earlier page; same race exists between addMembers/removeMember reloads and pagination; no request token/sequence guard

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces async pagination/actions that call `group.findMembers()` without any request sequencing or cancellation. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `next`/`previous` update `group.offset` and immediately `return group.findMembers()`. `findMembers()` performs `Discourse.ajax(...)` and in `.then(...)` unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members: ... })` from the response. If multiple requests are in-flight (e.g., clicking next twice quickly, or a pagination request overlapping with the `addMembers`/`removeMember` reload which also calls `self.findMembers()`), a slower older response can arrive last and overwrite `members/offset` with stale data, reverting the UI to an earlier page. The diff shows no token/sequence guard to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: create in admin/groups_controller.rb only assigns name and visible, silently dropping the alias_level param that the client sends and the new-group form renders, so groups are created with the default alias level

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create, the new code only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` from top-level params and never reads/assigns `alias_level` (diff shows no `group.alias_level = ...`). Meanwhile the client now sends `alias_level` on create via `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` and the form renders an alias-level combo box, so the server will ignore the user-selected alias level and persist the default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: PATCH API regression in admin/groups_controller.rb update — the old update_patch dispatch supporting the changes:{add/delete} incremental API was removed; new update unconditionally reads params[:group], which is nil for PATCH requests, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500, breaking existing API consumers/plugins

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old PATCH-specific incremental membership update path (`update_patch` and the `request.patch?` dispatch are gone), so PATCH requests with `changes:{add/delete}` would no longer be handled. However, the finding’s core claim that the new `update` “unconditionally reads params[:group]” and will raise `NoMethodError` on PATCH is not supported by the diff: the new `update` reads top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` only, and never references `params[:group]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: group_member.hbs renders the remove (×) link even for automatic groups because the template's context is the member (a Discourse.User), not the group, so 'automatic' resolves to undefined; additionally removeMember's promise chain has no failure handler, so the server's 422 rejection is silently swallowed

adjudication.rationale: The claim that `group_member.hbs` will always render the remove link because `automatic` resolves to `undefined` is not verifiable from the diff. The member rows are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and in Ember/Discourse itemView templates can still resolve properties from the parent controller/context; the diff does not show that `automatic` becomes inaccessible in the item view. The second point (422 rejection being “silently swallowed”) is also not directly supported by the diff: `removeMember` ultimately calls `Discourse.ajax(...)` and lacks an explicit failure handler, but whether that results in a silent failure depends on global/ajax error handling not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), a direct join-table delete that bypasses GroupUser callbacks (e.g. counter-cache maintenance of user_count, leaving it stale) and silently returns success when user_id is not actually a member

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff changed removal logic to `group.users.delete(user_id)` (then `group.save`). This bypasses any domain-specific removal method (the previous codepaths used `group.remove(user)`), and `delete` on an association will no-op if the user isn’t a member, so the action can return `success_json` even when nothing was removed. However, the claim about “bypassing GroupUser callbacks/counter-cache leaving user_count stale” is not directly verifiable from this diff (no join model/callbacks/counter-cache behavior is shown), and idempotent deletes may be acceptable behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: addMembers and removeMember in admin-group.js.es6 have no failure handlers — 422, 403, or network errors are swallowed with no message, leaving the UI unresponsive-looking after mutation attempts

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new actions `addMembers` and `removeMember` call `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` / `removeMember(...)` without any `.catch`/failure callback (and `addMembers` doesn’t even `return` the promise). The model methods in `group.js` perform `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` but also lack explicit error handling. The diff therefore supports the specific review concern that mutation failures (e.g., 422 from `can_not_modify_automatic`) are not handled at this call site; however, the claim that errors are “swallowed” and the UI becomes “unresponsive-looking” can’t be strictly verified from the diff alone because there may be global AJAX error handling elsewhere.
